summary: Tim Stevens argues that tires are essential for safety but also a major, underappreciated source of pollution, shedding millions of tons of wear particles and toxins like 6PPD-quinone. Manufacturers are responding with renewable materials such as guayule rubber and rice-husk silica, longer-lasting tires, retreading, and future concepts like non-pneumatic and wireless-charging tires. Experts caution that regulation and research are needed so that cutting wear mass doesn't make compounds more toxic.
one_line: Tires pollute through wear particles and toxins like 6PPD-quinone, while manufacturers pursue renewable materials, retreading and new designs to cut their environmental impact.
key_facts: Imperial College London researchers say cars and trucks emit 6 million tons of tire wear particles every year into air, land and water.
Nearly 250 million tires are disposed of annually in North America, roughly half of which are burned.
Bridgestone's guayule rubber, grown in the Southwestern US, was used in IndyCar road course tires this year; hevea trees are primarily grown in Southeast Asia.
Yokohama's Advan A005 tire, debuted at last year's Pikes Peak International Hill Climb, contains 33 percent sustainable materials.
Michelin shod Porsche's prototype electric GT4 e-Performance racer with tires said to be 53 percent renewable.
Dunlop promises 40 percent renewable tires by the end of this decade and 100 percent by 2050; Bridgestone's Turanza EV is made of 50 percent renewable and recycled materials.
Per Bridgestone's Bill Niaura, natural rubber, synthetic rubber, and fillers (carbon black and silica) each make up about 25 percent of tire materials.
Goodyear now uses silica sourced from a rice processing byproduct called husk ash; silica replacing carbon black improves wet performance and reduces rolling resistance.
A Pew Charitable Trusts report found 78 percent of ocean microplastics are synthetic tire rubber.
A 2020 University of Washington Center for Urban Waters study linked 6PPD-quinone, formed when 6PPD reacts with ozone, to the decline of coho salmon.
California regulation will require tire sellers to eliminate 6PPD or research alternatives over the next five years; Euro 7 will cap tire wear particles.
Typical tire wear life was about 20,000 miles in the early 1970s, while 80,000-mile warranties are now relatively common.
Bridgestone's Bandag retread business has saved 300 million tires from being thrown out, worth roughly 4 billion gallons of oil.
Michelin's non-pneumatic Uptis tire could reduce tire replacements by 20 percent.
Bridgestone's Wireless In-Wheel Tire concept, shown at the Japan Mobility Show, puts inductive charging receiving coils in the tires of an EV.
